supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Smoking Dark Star, epic The Other One, tight acoustic sets
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a soaring Dark Star jam and an expansive The Other One sequence, framed by two acoustic halves that let Pigpen’s organ shine. Jerry’s guitar work is on fire, Phil lays down thunderous bass, while Mickey adds depth to the improvisations.
ai_show_review.review:
May 15, 1970 at the Fillmore East captures the Dead in a rare balance of folk‑leaning acoustics and full‑throttle psychedelia. The early acoustic set moves from “Don’t Ease Me In” through “Candyman,” letting Pigpen’s organ color the mix before the band launches into a ripping electric second set. Highlights include an incendiary “The Other One” that showcases Jerry’s flawless tone, pedal‑steel flourishes and Phil’s thunderous bass, while Mickey’s percussion adds extra depth to the jam. The encore “New Minglewood Blues” closes the night on a high note despite a few over‑squealing guitar moments. Both soundboard sources are crystal clear – one described as pristine with studio‑like fidelity, the other as good with only minor dropouts – making this performance both historically significant and sonically rewarding.

The recording recommended for listening is the “early‑late” SBD (gd70-05-15.early-late.sbd.97.sbeok.shnf), praised for its pristine capture and excellent mix that brings out every nuance of the band’s interplay. Whether you’re chasing the legendary Dark Star stretch, the ferocious “The Other One,” or the nuanced acoustic interludes, this show stands as a benchmark of the Dead’s 1970 live prowess.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: Both recordings are marked as positive and repeatedly praise the same high‑impact moments – Dark Star, The Other One, Attics Of My Life, and strong acoustic work. Consistent language such as “smoking,” “epic,” and “flawless” across sources signals a strong positive consensus, warranting a +1.6 sentiment boost.

best_recording.reason: Pristine soundboard capture with studio‑like fidelity; minimal hiss and dropouts, delivering the clearest representation of the performance.

key_highlights: Smoking Dark Star jam that stretches into cosmic territory
Epic The Other One sequence with powerful dual drumming
Two acoustic sets showcasing Pigpen’s organ and folk‑leaning repertoire

band_performance.Jerry: Soaring guitar work, flawless vocals and even pedal‑steel on the NRPS numbers; perfect tone leading the fierce The Other One jam.
band_performance.Phil: Thunderous and tight bass, especially during The Other One and Dark Star jams; occasionally harder to hear on acoustic sets.
band_performance.Bob: Strong rhythm/lead contributions with a notable “Uncle John” jam within Dark Star, adding depth to the improvisations.
band_performance.Mickey: Percussion adds depth to Dark Star and overall drumming is solid throughout the show.
band_performance.Billy: Solid drumming that anchors the jams; no major complaints across recordings.
